candidates.designation: tau Ceti e (Feng et al. 2017, Table 5; first suspected as the 168 d signal of Tuomi et al. 2013)
candidates.tier_reason: Figueira et al. 2025 (ESPRESSO GTO, 10 cm/s-level study) say the 3.93 M_E planet at 162 d 'should have been detected with our analysis' and 'Our results do not support' it. NASA Exoplanet Archive has removed it as a published refutation. exoplanet.eu still carries it as 'Controversial' (updated 2026-04-26) and OEC as 'Confirmed'. Best current reading: probably not a planet; one non-detection paper, not an activity/alias demonstration, so I left it as a candidate rather than an exclusion. Writer may prefer to exclude it (see considered_not_added entry).
candidates.orbit_flags: RV only (HARPS+AAPS+HIRES reanalysis with MA noise model). K = 0.55 m/s. P, e, a, Msini from Feng+2017 Table 5 (1%-99% intervals, not 1-sigma). No inclination; debris-disk inclination ~30 deg would double the mass if coplanar (Feng+2017 text). Not recovered by ESPRESSO (Figueira+2025), removed by NASA as refuted; exoplanet.eu Controversial.
candidates.reference: Feng et al. 2017, AJ 154, 135, 'Color difference makes a difference: four planet candidates around tau Ceti', Table 5; contested by Figueira et al. 2025, A&A 700, A174

considered_not_added.name: tau Cet b, c, d (Tuomi et al. 2013)
considered_not_added.reason: withdrawn/superseded: the 13.9, 35.4 and 94 d signals of Tuomi et al. 2013 (A&A 551, A79, arXiv:1212.4277) were not recovered by the same team's reanalysis (Feng et al. 2017, AJ 154, 135, arXiv:1708.02051), which reports only 20.0, 49.3, 160 and 642 d signals. OEC lists b, c and d as 'Retracted planet candidate'. Not in NASA or exoplanet.eu. exoplanet.eu still lists b, c, d as 'Candidate' (pages tau_cet_b--1234, tau_cet_c--1235, tau_cet_d--1236, not updated since 2021); Figueira et al. 2025 report ESPRESSO sensitivity to 1.7 M_E for P < 100 d with no such signals, and b/c/d had Msini 2.0-3.6 M_E.

considered_not_added.name: rho CrB d
considered_not_added.reason: refuted: Zhao et al. 2026 (ApJS 282, 71; arXiv:2601.02296) correct EXPRES instrumental drifts and state the correction 'removes a spurious planet d signal' in the rho CrB time series. NASA lists it under 'Planets With Published Refutations' citing Zhao et al. 2026. rho CrB d was announced by Brewer et al. 2023 (AJ 166, 46).

considered_not_added.name: ups And e
considered_not_added.reason: refuted: instrumental. McArthur et al. 2014 (ApJ 795, 41, Sect. 3.1.1) show the 3848 d signal of Curiel et al. 2011 was created by neglected gamma offsets in the Lick velocities: 'This instrumental signal in the data created by neglected gamma offsets was identified as a fourth planet with period of 3848 days ... in Curiel et al. (2011)'. NASA lists ups And e under 'Planets With Published Refutations' (2014ApJ...795...41M). Catalogues disagree: OEC 'Controversial', exoplanet.eu still 'Confirmed' (ups_and_ae--781, updated 2024-07-21). Writer may wish to note the exoplanet.eu status.

considered_not_added.name: 61 Vir d
considered_not_added.reason: already on confirmed tab (row 357), but contested: Rosenthal et al. 2021 (CLS I, ApJS 255, 8, App. G.1 and Table 7) designate the 124 d signal 'a yearly systematic' (HIRES PSF parameters periodic at 1 yr and correlated with RVs), cause code N; it is omitted from their Table 3 planet catalog. Harada et al. 2025 (SPORES-HWO II, AJ 170, 343) recover it at 123.15 d, 10.9 M_E Msini (NASA ps). Not added; flagged for the writer in case the confirmed row deserves a caveat.
